course.name: Public Speaking
course.description: Comprehensive 12-week NPTEL curriculum covering the art of oratory, classical canons of rhetoric, audience psychology, managing speech anxiety, non-verbal cues, voice modulation, elocution, humor, meeting leadership, and digital communication.

weeks.title: Introduction to Public Speaking & The Canons of Rhetoric
weeks.coreFocus: Understanding speech as an acquired craft, active listening essentials, ethical communication, and Quintilian's five canons of rhetoric.
topics: Public speaking as a learned and acquirable skill
Ralph Waldo Emerson on the persuasive power of speech
Rhetorical devices and eliciting audience emotional resonance
Active listening vs. passive hearing
Ethics in public speaking: Avoiding ethnocentrism, alienation, and plagiarism types
Quintilian's Five Canons: Invention, Disposition, Style, Memorization, Delivery
weeks.keyTakeaway: Effective public speaking is not an innate gift but a systematic discipline rooted in Quintilian's five canons and ethical audience engagement.

examStrategy.title: 💡 High-Yield Strategy for NPTEL Public Speaking Exam
points: Assignment Heavy: Nearly 80% of the NPTEL Public Speaking exam questions are derived directly from the 12 weekly assignment quizzes.

Theorists & Frameworks: Memorize key theorists — Sperber & Wilson (Relevance), Albert Mehrabian (7-38-55%), Edward Hall (Proxemics), Paul Watzlawick (Pragmatics), Roman Jakobson (6 Functions), and Hersey-Blanchard (Situational Leadership).

Multiple Select Questions (MSQs): Weeks 4, 7, 8, 11, and 12 feature questions where multiple options are correct (e.g., types of dramatic speeches, soliloquy features, interview biases). Practice identifying all valid options.

tips.heading: Master the 5 Canons of Rhetoric
tips.text: Quintilian's classical canons (Invention, Disposition, Style, Memory, Delivery) form the theoretical core of Weeks 1 and 2.

tips.heading: Memorize Theorists & Seminal Concepts
tips.text: High question frequency on Sperber & Wilson (Relevance), Albert Mehrabian (7-38-55%), Edward Hall (Proxemics), Paul Watzlawick (Pragmatics), Roman Jakobson (6 Functions), and Hersey-Blanchard (Situational Leadership).

tips.heading: Watch for MSQs (Multiple Select Questions)
tips.text: Weeks 4, 7, 8, 11, and 12 feature multiple-choice questions requiring you to select all correct options (e.g. dramatic speeches, soliloquy features, interview biases).

tips.heading: Distinguish Technical Terms
tips.text: Be clear on differences: Agenda vs. Minutes; Transitions vs. Signposts; Cadence vs. Accent/Stress; Digression vs. Distraction; Kinesics (Birdwhistell) vs. Proxemics (Hall).
